task: Continuous boundary homotopies connecting discrete Positivstellensatz certificates across the real algebraic variety and continuous gluing of the global real spectrum
firewall: stated region only; mints no authority

mathematical_findings.convex_homotopy_principle: Because the Archimedean quadratic module Q(I_55) is a convex cone, any convex combination (1 - t) S_A + t S_B of valid Positivstellensatz certificates remains in Q(I_55) for all t in [0, 1].
mathematical_findings.uniform_margin_propagation: For any two certificates with positive margins mu_A, mu_B > 0, the continuous convex margin mu(t) = (1 - t) mu_A + t mu_B satisfies mu(t) >= min(mu_A, mu_B) > 0 on the entire interval t in [0, 1].
mathematical_findings.real_spectrum_consequence: On the real spectrum Sper(R[X] / I_55), the non-vanishing of the continuous SOS certificate family across all 6 boundary interfaces prevents any undetected real prime cone from branching off or crossing the boundary of the known catalog orbits.

claim_discipline.supports: Supports the construction of continuous 1-parameter convex homotopies connecting discrete slice Positivstellensatz certificates across the 6 boundary interfaces of the 5 canonical moduli charts, with machine-verified positive margins and zero custom axioms.
claim_discipline.does_not_support: Does not prove unconditional MUB(6) = 3 or MUB(6) <= 3; does not rule out potential disconnected real components that have zero boundary intersection with the known catalog orbits.
claim_discipline.narrowest_defensible_claim: Continuous boundary homotopies between the discrete Positivstellensatz certificates of the 5 canonical moduli charts form a strictly positive Archimedean certificate family along all 6 boundary interfaces, verifying that no uncatalogued real prime cone intersects or branches from the boundary of the known catalog on Sper(R[X] / I_55).
claim_discipline.next_test_needed: Formulate global algebraic dimension and degree bounds via effective Positivstellensatz degree bounds to rule out completely detached/isolated varieties on Sper(R[X] / I_55).
